Making sense of the world is an incredibly difficult task.

To do it perfectly, without ever making any mistakes, would be far too slow and expensive. So the brains of humans (and other creatures) have to guess and approximate, as best as they can. Because humans live very different lives compared to other creatures, our brains make these best guesses in very different ways. This results in humans and other creatures seeing the world with very different eyes, having very different behaviors, and very different ways of solving problems.

To a lesser degree, the same can be said about men and women: Since our roles in life are and always have been very different, it only makes sense that our brains would perform their best guesses about the nature of the world in different ways.

Both men and women can learn about mental tools like logic and statistics, to help us improve our guesses. But underneath those tools will always be our natural way of guessing, and any models built on top of it will be subject to its limitations.

Men tend to think by means of heuristics. We seek patterns, we simplify, we create models. We focus on trend lines, and not the individual points that shape them. We do this by default, without ever learning about it or even knowing what those terms mean. Science and engineering are built on top of this. Or, rather, emerged from this, as distilled models with well-defined rules. Since logic and statistics are tools created by and for science and engineering, they also sit on top of heuristics quite comfortably, and work well together with it, to make better informed judgments. We derive confidence that our ideas are right from how well they fit those models.

Women tend to think by means of linguistics. They talk (a lot), to exchange stories, about specific people and specific events. They focus on the individual points, and not on the trend lines they form. This is what helps them think and make sense of the world. The more a story stands out, the more unusual it is, the more rousing and emotional, the more compelling its lesson will be. This is how they exchange ideas and judgments, to then form their own opinion... by consensus. Without this, they quickly grow anxious and frustrated, feeling lost and without a sense of direction. This is why they tend to be glued to social media these days; it is a constant stream of stories about people and events, with built-in feedback mechanisms to find the most talked and agreed upon ones. They derive confidence that their ideas are right from that consensus.

Speaking of heuristics: The above is a model. As always, there will be exceptions. Exceptions do not disprove the rule. They are to be expected. There always have and always will be some percentage of women who lean more towards heuristics, as well as some percentage of men who lean more towards linguistics. And most will fall somewhere in between, using both to some degree. But, generally speaking, most men will depend heavily on heuristic thinking and most women will depend heavily on linguistic thinking. And be will therefore be moved by the most compelling models or stories, respectively.
